speaker: edmund_shakespeare
text: Stand back from the rain-barrel. When the king comes out of the wash-house, thou art to kneel and offer him the bowl.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: Why must I be the woman? I was the horse yesterday.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: Thou wast a bad horse. Thou sat on the well-curb in the middle of it and ate an apple.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: A horse must bait when the noise stops. I am the Soldan today, and Edmund may kneel to me.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Whoever has the crown is the Soldan. Whose is the pewter colander?

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: The colander is the kitchen's. If either of them dents it, there will be a tragedy before supper that I do not have to act.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: Watch. I take him along the flank, and the lath never touches the rim.

speaker: edmund_shakespeare
text: Holla, ye pampered jades of Asia! What, can ye draw but twenty miles a day?

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: Then I am the horse again, and you said I was a queen.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: Now the king is besieged in a basket, and nobody lets him out unless he pays.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Hold. Yield him, or I shall split before the ransom is set.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: If a king is in a clothes-basket with a colander on his head, is that a comedy or a history?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is a history until the colander falls off. After that it is a jig, and the jig is not mine.

speaker: edmund_shakespeare
text: Take it off. It has wet parsley in the holes. Do the end, Will, where the horse is gone.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Not the end, and not today. Breathe from thy ribs, not thy throat, or thou wilt be hoarse before supper. The colander is a colander.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: Then Father is the messenger, and if he speaks more than four lines we take his shoes.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: Four lines, and no book-words.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Great Soldan on the wash-house tub, release my brother from the pot. I bring two windfall pippins here, which is the whole exchequer got.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: That was four lines. One pippin is bruised.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: That is the wasp-apple from this morning. The ransom is bit.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Your mother is in the passage. Give me the colander before she sees parsley on a collar.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Tomorrow after the Cross. All three of us, up past the Rother Market.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: All three, after the stall, and not a lath among us.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: The lath stays on the peg. We take you as far as the last barn.

speaker: judith_shakespeare
text: And I am not the horse on the way back.

speaker: edmund_shakespeare
text: I was loud enough. I am not asking to be loud in London. I am asking to be heard as far as the barrel.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The barrel heard thee. That is the house you have today. Breathe, and give Joan her colander.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Colander. Now. The pageant is over when the parsley is over.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: The count for tomorrow is still twenty houses, and still nobody hurt. The basket was a different kingdom.
